title.value: Considerations and recommendations from the ISMRM Diffusion Study Group for preclinical diffusion MRI: Part 3 — Ex vivo imaging: data processing, comparisons with microscopy, and tractography
title.justification: The title of the paper is prominently located at the beginning of the document and concisely sums up the main focus and scope of the research work.
title.quote: Considerations and recommendations from the ISMRM Diffusion Study Group for preclinical diffusion MRI: Part 3 — Ex vivo imaging: data processing, comparisons with microscopy, and tractography

analysis.description: This paper provides guidelines and recommendations for preclinical diffusion MRI focusing specifically on ex vivo imaging. It addresses the processes of image pre-processing, data processing, model fitting, tractography, and comparisons with microscopy.

type.justification: The paper provides practical guidelines and recommendations based on experiments and existing practices for preclinical diffusion MRI, which indicates an empirical study.
type.quote: This work concludes a 3-part series of recommendations and considerations for preclinical dMRI. Herein, we describe best practices for dMRI of ex vivo tissue, with a focus on image pre-processing, data processing and model fitting, and tractography.

name.justification: The paper is focused on diffusion MRI, which is a critical area within the broader field of Medical Imaging, particularly emphasizing preclinical imaging for diffusion studies.
name.quote: Preclinical diffusion MRI (dMRI) has proven value in methods development and validation, characterizing the biological basis of diffusion phenomena, and comparative anatomy.

name.justification: The paper discusses neuroimaging topics such as brain connectivity and tissue microstructure probing through diffusion MRI.
name.quote: Preclinical imaging is essential for methodological development and validation, characterizing the biological basis of diffusion phenomena, and comparative anatomy.

name.justification: The paper details methods for comparing MRI data with microscopy at different resolutions and configurations, which is a significant field in the study.
name.quote: We describe best practices for dMRI of ex vivo tissue, with a focus on image pre-processing, data processing and model fitting, and tractography. Finally, we give... related to comparisons with histology, and ex vivo fiber tractography.

name.justification: The paper mentions the NODDI model as an existing model adapted in the study of ex vivo diffusion MRI data.
name.quote: A typical example of this is an ‘ex vivo flag’ in the original implementation and source code of the NODDI model which changed the assumed fixed diffusivity from 1.7E-6 mm ^{2} /s to 0.6E-6 mm ^{2} /s.
